title: Impact of Pharmaceutical Patent Approval on Company Returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Event Study methodology is appropriate here. We'll calculate abnormal returns as the difference between actual returns and expected returns (using CAPM: expected return = beta × market return). The key assumption is that the market efficiently incorporates new information, and any systematic deviation from expected returns around the patent approval date reflects the causal impact of the event.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s61_data.csv")

# Calculate abnormal returns using CAPM
data$abnormal_ret <- data$ret - (data$beta * data$mkt_ret)

# Calculate cumulative abnormal returns (CAR) for each stock
car_data <- data %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  arrange(event_day) %>%
  mutate(car = cumsum(abnormal_ret)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Calculate average abnormal returns and average CAR across all stocks by event day
event_analysis <- car_data %>%
  group_by(event_day) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_abnormal_ret = mean(abnormal_ret),
    avg_car = mean(car),
    se_abnormal_ret = sd(abnormal_ret) / sqrt(n()),
    se_car = sd(car) / sqrt(n()),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

# Calculate key event windows
# CAR for event window [-1, +1]
car_window_1 <- car_data %>%
  filter(event_day >= -1 & event_day <= 1) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(car_window = sum(abnormal_ret), .groups = 'drop')

cat("CAR[-1,+1] Summary:\n")
cat("Mean CAR:", round(mean(car_window_1$car_window), 4), "\n")
cat("Standard Error:", round(sd(car_window_1$car_window) / sqrt(nrow(car_window_1)), 4), "\n")
t_stat_1 <- mean(car_window_1$car_window) / (sd(car_window_1$car_window) / sqrt(nrow(car_window_1)))
cat("t-statistic:", round(t_stat_1, 3), "\n")
cat("p-value:", round(2 * (1 - pt(abs(t_stat_1), df = nrow(car_window_1) - 1)), 4), "\n")

# CAR for event window [0, +2] 
car_window_2 <- car_data %>%
  filter(event_day >= 0 & event_day <= 2) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(car_window = sum(abnormal_ret), .groups = 'drop')

cat("\nCAR[0,+2] Summary:\n")
cat("Mean CAR:", round(mean(car_window_2$car_window), 4), "\n")
cat("Standard Error:", round(sd(car_window_2$car_window) / sqrt(nrow(car_window_2)), 4), "\n")
t_stat_2 <- mean(car_window_2$car_window) / (sd(car_window_2$car_window) / sqrt(nrow(car_window_2)))
cat("t-statistic:", round(t_stat_2, 3), "\n")
cat("p-value:", round(2 * (1 - pt(abs(t_stat_2), df = nrow(car_window_2) - 1)), 4), "\n")

# Event day (day 0) abnormal return
day_0_ar <- car_data %>%
  filter(event_day == 0) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_ar = mean(abnormal_ret),
    se_ar = sd(abnormal_ret) / sqrt(n())
  )

cat("\nEvent Day (Day 0) Abnormal Return:\n")
cat("Mean AR:", round(day_0_ar$mean_ar, 4), "\n")
cat("Standard Error:", round(day_0_ar$se_ar, 4), "\n")
t_stat_0 <- day_0_ar$mean_ar / day_0_ar$se_ar
cat("t-statistic:", round(t_stat_0, 3), "\n")
cat("p-value:", round(2 * (1 - pt(abs(t_stat_0), df = 79)), 4), "\n")

# Robustness check: Test for pre-event drift
pre_event <- car_data %>%
  filter(event_day >= -5 & event_day <= -1) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(pre_car = sum(abnormal_ret), .groups = 'drop')

cat("\nRobustness Check - Pre-event CAR[-5,-1]:\n")
cat("Mean Pre-event CAR:", round(mean(pre_event$pre_car), 4), "\n")
t_stat_pre <- mean(pre_event$pre_car) / (sd(pre_event$pre_car) / sqrt(nrow(pre_event)))
cat("t-statistic:", round(t_stat_pre, 3), "\n")
cat("p-value:", round(2 * (1 - pt(abs(t_stat_pre), df = nrow(pre_event) - 1)), 4), "\n")

# Plot the average CAR over time
plot(event_analysis$event_day, event_analysis$avg_car, 
     type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "blue",
     xlab = "Event Day", ylab = "Average CAR",
     main = "Average Cumulative Abnormal Returns Around Patent Approval")
abline(v = 0, col = "red", lty = 2)
abline(h = 0, col = "gray", lty = 1)
grid()
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a positive and statistically significant CAR around the patent approval event, with the magnitude likely in the range of 2-8%. The sign should be positive because patent approval represents valuable intellectual property that provides competitive advantages and future revenue streams. The impact should be most pronounced on the event day (day 0) and the day after (day +1), as markets digest the news. Pre-event abnormal returns should be close to zero, supporting the validity of the event study methodology.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare stock returns before and after patent approval.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Patent approvals lead to a significant increase in drug-company CAR.
